description: D-01 — Platform Overview. Default landing page for operators. Answers: Is the entire back_vibes platform healthy right now? Covers HTTP API, queue workers, scheduler, Smart Home business pipeline, and Collector infrastructure health in a single view. Use specialized dashboards (D-02 through D-07) for deep investigation.

panels.description: Fraction of HTTP requests that did NOT result in a server-side error (5xx, outcome=server_error). Healthy steady-state: > 99%. Below 95% is critical — navigate to D-05 HTTP API to identify the failing route, then Tempo for trace detail.
panels.title: HTTP Availability

panels.description: Fraction of completed queue job attempts (excluding retried/released in-progress) that succeeded. Healthy steady-state: > 95%. Below 90% warrants investigation — navigate to D-04 Queue Workers to identify the failing job class.
panels.title: Queue Health

panels.description: Scheduled event execution rate (all outcomes). Healthy: matches the registered schedule count per minute (~1/min per event for a 1-minute schedule). Zero indicates the scheduler loop has stopped — navigate to D-06 Scheduler to investigate.
panels.title: Scheduler Running

panels.description: Fraction of Smart Home action executions that succeeded (outcome=success). Healthy steady-state: > 95%. A drop below 90% is critical — navigate to D-02 Smart Home to identify the failing provider or outcome class.
panels.title: Smart Home Health

panels.description: OpenTelemetry Collector process status. 1 = up, 0 = down. Healthy: always 1. If the Collector is down, all telemetry (metrics, traces, logs) will stop flowing — navigate to D-07 Infrastructure for detail. Note: this metric is Collector-scoped and does not filter by $environment.
panels.title: Collector Up

panels.description: Total application-side OTLP export failures in the last hour (ixora_telemetry_export_failed_total). Non-zero means back_vibes failed to deliver telemetry to the Collector. Healthy: 0. Any non-zero value requires investigation — navigate to D-07 Infrastructure to confirm Collector is healthy.
panels.title: Telemetry Export Failures

panels.description: Total Smart Home dispatch calls (outcome=dispatched) in the selected time window. A dispatch call enqueues actions for execution. This is the top-of-funnel business metric. Low volume in expected automation windows may indicate the scheduler or HTTP trigger is not working — check D-06 or D-05.
panels.title: Smart Home Dispatches

panels.description: Current Smart Home action success rate (outcome=success / total). Healthy: > 95%. This is the primary business health KPI — a drop here affects automation reliability directly. Navigate to D-02 Smart Home for full breakdown by provider and outcome.
panels.title: Action Success Rate

panels.description: Current Smart Home action failure rate (outcome=failure or unknown / total). Does NOT include unsupported — that is a distinct business outcome. Above 5% warrants investigation in D-02. Note: ixora_queue_job_total{outcome=success} does NOT measure this — Queue success and Action success are orthogonal signals (Phase 7B.4.5 §8.3).
panels.title: Action Failure Rate

panels.description: Smart Home action execution P95 latency in milliseconds. Healthy: P95 < 2000 ms. Measures the full execution segment including the HTTP call to the provider (e.g. Home Assistant). A rising P95 suggests provider degradation — navigate to D-02 Performance section for P50/P95/P99 breakdown.
panels.title: Action p95 Latency

panels.description: Smart Home action success and failure rates over time. The success rate should remain above 95% in steady state. Use this panel to correlate drops with deployments, provider incidents, or scheduler changes. For full breakdown by provider and outcome, navigate to D-02 Smart Home.

links.title: D-02 Smart Home — full business detail

panels.title: Business Health Over Time

panels.description: Total HTTP request rate over time (all outcomes, all routes). Healthy: matches expected traffic volume for the environment. A sudden sustained drop may indicate the API is not receiving traffic or the Collector is down. For per-route and error-rate breakdown, navigate to D-05 HTTP API.
panels.title: HTTP Requests/s

panels.description: HTTP 5xx server error rate over time (outcome=server_error). Healthy: near 0%. A spike above 1% is the primary alerting signal for the HTTP layer. For per-route breakdown and trace drill-down, navigate to D-05 HTTP API.
panels.title: HTTP Error Rate

panels.description: Queue job processing rate per second, split by queue. Queues: smart-home (Smart Home action jobs), push (push notification jobs), default (all other jobs). A drop on smart-home queue while dispatches continue indicates growing queue depth — workers may be down. Navigate to D-04 Queue Workers for full detail.
panels.title: Queue Throughput (by Queue)

panels.description: Number of queue jobs currently in-flight (active). Healthy: a small positive number matching worker concurrency. Sustained high values with no corresponding throughput increase may indicate stuck workers. Navigate to D-04 Queue Workers for duration and failure context.
panels.title: Active Queue Jobs

panels.description: Scheduler event execution rate over time by outcome. Healthy: consistent rate matching registered schedule count. outcome=overlap_prevented is normal (idempotency guard). outcome=failed should remain at 0. For batch duration, skipped details, and Smart Home cross-domain view, navigate to D-06 Scheduler.
panels.title: Scheduler Executions (by Outcome)

panels.description: OpenTelemetry Collector process status. 1 = up, 0 = down. If the Collector is down, all telemetry ceases — every other panel in this dashboard will show stale data. Navigate to D-07 Infrastructure for process memory, CPU, and export pipeline detail. Note: Collector-scoped metric, not filtered by $environment.
panels.title: Collector Process

panels.description: Prometheus process status (scraped as a Prometheus target). 1 = up, 0 = down. If Prometheus is down, all metric-based panels will show stale or no data. Note: Prometheus-scoped metric, not filtered by $environment.
panels.title: Prometheus Process

panels.description: OpenTelemetry Collector resident memory (RSS) in bytes. A continuously growing RSS may indicate a memory leak in the Collector pipeline. Navigate to D-07 Infrastructure for full Collector health detail. Note: Collector-scoped metric, not filtered by $environment.
panels.title: Collector Memory

panels.description: OpenTelemetry Collector CPU usage rate (fraction of a CPU core). Healthy: low and stable. A sustained high value may indicate a processing bottleneck in the Collector pipeline. Navigate to D-07 Infrastructure for full resource detail. Note: Collector-scoped metric, not filtered by $environment.
panels.title: Collector CPU

panels.description: Collector export failure rates over time for spans (Tempo), log records (Loki), and metric points (Prometheus Remote Write). Any non-zero values indicate data loss in the telemetry pipeline. Healthy: all lines at 0. Navigate to D-07 Infrastructure for queue depth and detailed pipeline panels.
panels.title: Collector Export Errors

panels.description: Prometheus Remote Write pipeline: metric points sent vs failed per second. Healthy: sent > 0, failed = 0. A non-zero failed rate means metrics are being dropped before reaching Prometheus storage — all application metric panels will show stale or incomplete data. Navigate to D-07 Infrastructure for queue depth detail.
panels.title: Remote Write Status (Metrics)
